claims.text: The target material consists of nearly equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
In situ aberration-corrected STEM with HAADF imaging and a heating stage can directly observe temperature-induced atomic rearrangements in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
The proposed STEM method can directly observe elemental redistribution in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Observing atomic rearrangement and redistribution by this method would validate the role of thermodynamic contributions in the thermal stability of the nanoparticles.
The as-prepared AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a uniform, well-mixed, homogeneous elemental distribution.
The as-prepared AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have a defined and uniform morphology.
The experiment will progressively heat the sample in situ under high vacuum to approximately 700–1000 K.
Local lattice distortions, elemental segregation, and defect formation mediate temperature-driven structural changes in the nanoparticles.
Increasing temperature creates thermodynamic driving forces that induce atomic diffusion in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Temperature-induced atomic diffusion causes elemental redistribution within AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Heating-induced redistribution changes the lattice structure and produces compositional or phase boundaries.
Real-time STEM imaging will reveal progressive lattice distortions during heating.
Real-time imaging and compositional mapping will reveal progressive elemental segregation during heating.
The observed structural and compositional changes will correlate with increasing temperature.
The room-temperature as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles exhibit a stable lattice structure.
Beam-induced artifacts may affect the observed structural changes.
The exact transition temperatures and extent of redistribution may depend on synthesis and experimental conditions.
EDS elemental mapping can monitor elemental distributions during the heating experiment.
